title: refactor(ci): consolidate node workflows, speed up lint/test, and improve release automation
author: Sana Patel
release_notes: Consolidated CI workflows, upgraded Node to 20 in actions, improved caching and concurrency to reduce build time; release automation moved to release-please with improved tagging and changelog generation.
description: Motivation: our repo has accumulated many duplicated GitHub Actions workflows (per-package lint/test/release), leading to slow feedback loops, inconsistent job matrices, and fragile release automation. This PR consolidates lint/test/release workflows across the monorepo, upgrades standard CI environment to Node 20, applies cache and concurrency improvements, and migrates release automation from a custom drafter script to release-please. Changes are intended to reduce CI run-time, reduce flakiness, and improve release traceability. What I changed: 1) New .github/workflows/ci.yml that unifies lint, unit-test, and integration-test jobs with a matrix that scopes jobs by affected packages to avoid running everything on every push. 2) Replaced multiple repo-specific release workflows with .github/workflows/release-please.yml and removed the in-repo release-drafter config. release-please is configured to tag by package and create changelogs per release. 3) Upgraded all Node JS runner versions in workflows to node:20 and consolidated action versions (actions/checkout@v4, actions/cache@v4). 4) Introduced persistent npm/cache and docker layer caching; restored concurrency groups to prevent duplicate runs on rapid pushes. 5) Linted and updated workflow permissions and OIDC usages to follow security best practices. 6) Updated dev dependencies in package.json across top-level workspaces: eslint@8.x -> eslint@8.41.0, typescript@5.3.3 -> 5.4.2, jest@29.x -> 29.6.1; fixed resulting types/lint errors. 7) Small test harness fixes: stabilized a flaky integration test by increasing a timeout and adding deterministic seed. 8) CI infra docs: updated docs/ci.md with workflow layout and troubleshooting. Checklist: [x] Consolidate workflows and preserve existing lint/test coverage. [x] Keep release automation backwards-compatible where possible. [x] Run full CI in a staging branch and validate release tags. [x] Update developer docs. Testing: ran full CI on a feature branch (staging/ci-consolidation) including canary releases via release-please; validated package tagging and changelogs in a test repo. Rollout plan: merge to main, monitor release-please runs for next 48 hours, revert release-please invocation if any regressions in tag generation. Notes: kept the legacy release-drafter/legacy-release.yml in .github/legacy/ to allow rollback for one week, after which it will be removed. See related tickets: ENG-4721 (ci consolidation), ENG-4723 (release automation), SUP-1287 (support flakiness report).

review_comments: Ethan Wong: Please add a migration note for any contributors using legacy release-drafter hooks. Reply (Sana): Added legacy note and placed the legacy workflow under .github/legacy/ for one-week rollback.

Lina Chen: The matrix looks good, but can we ensure tests run for changed packages only? Reply (Sana): Implemented affected-package detection using git diff and NX-like globs; fallback runs full test on non-detectable cases.

Carlos Ruiz: Are there permission changes for release workflow? Concern about token scopes. Reply (Sana): release-please uses minimal permissions; explicitly set write:packages only where needed and scoped GITHUB_TOKEN usage as documented.
Ethan Wong: CI cache key collisions observed in early run. Reply (Sana): Cache keys namespaced by runner OS and node version and added restore-keys fallback.
Lina Chen: Please run a dry-run release to validate tagging. Reply (Sana): Completed release-please dry-run against a test repo and included artifacts in the PR comments.
